svg.text: CALLOUT LEGEND · HOV = ON HOVER · CMT = ON COMMIT · L/G = UNDER
LOOP OR GRIP
Involvement spine, rotated
The one element that must not be cut. At 390px it
turns horizontal and docks under the sticky header:
still one continuous bar, still four labelled
segments, still summing to 100%. Q-A is answered
above the fold on a phone, before anything else is
read.
HOV
Not applicable — see callout 6.
CMT
Segments animate as on desktop.
L/G
Loop collapses a segment to a labelled sliver; Grip
inverts the order of magnitude, which is legible even
at 26px tall.
Accordion of four — all live, one at FULL
Four panels survive as an accordion: exactly one
expanded at FULL fidelity, three collapsed to 40px
strips that keep glyph, label, rank, a live
sparkline, and three numerals. Nothing is removed
from the simulation and nothing is shrunk below
legibility — the tier rule from S5 does all the work.
HOV
A collapsed strip still shows its delta during a
forecast.
CMT
All four step; the expanded one shows the full
change.
L/G
Grip auto-expands the inferior and collapses the
dominant, which is how the state announces itself on
a phone.
Collapsed strips carry deltas
The reason four panels survive a phone: a collapsed
strip does not need five readouts, it needs one
signed delta. During a forecast the three collapsed
strips each show a single number, which is enough to
answer “who pays?” without expanding anything.
HOV
Delta replaces the chevron.
CMT
Delta clears.
L/G
A bypassed function shows a dash rather than a zero.
Whole-Human dock
A 40px permanent dock above the action sheet carrying
the aggregate trace and four single-letter scalars.
The aggregate is never more than one tap away and
never off screen, preserving the part-and-whole rule
that the desktop band exists to serve.
HOV
CMT
Ticks with the rows.
L/G
The dock is where a state change is most visible on a
phone, because it never scrolls away.
Action sheet, peeked
A bottom sheet showing the top-ranked action, its
signature, and its likelihood. Dragging up reveals
all five. It occupies the thumb zone and it is the
only element that overlaps content.
HOV
CMT
Slide-up-to-commit, which cannot be triggered
accidentally by a scroll.
L/G
Generated alleviate/aggravate cards are sorted into
the sheet with their tags intact.
Press-and-hold replaces hover
The critical adaptation. There is no hover on a touch
device, so the forecast is bound to press-and-hold:
holding renders every forecast live, releasing
cancels and restores the resting screen exactly, and
committing requires a deliberate second gesture
(slide up). The hover contract — nothing spent,
nothing recorded, no beat consumed — is preserved
verbatim; only the input changes.
HOV
Hold to enter the forecast; the card labels itself
HOLDING.
CMT
Slide up while holding.
L/G
Identical in all states.
Sticky header keeps Q-C above the fold
Scenario identity, state chip, and both margin meters
compress into 82px and stay pinned. Distance-to-break
is the one readout that must never require scrolling,
on any viewport.
HOV
CMT
Margins step.
L/G
The chip inverts and the crossed margin reads IN.
Aggregate as a full sheet
Tapping the dock raises the S6 apparatus as a
full-height sheet rather than a route change. The
four keep ticking behind it, and dismissing returns
to the same beat — expansion is disclosure, not
navigation, exactly as on desktop.
HOV
CMT
L/G
The aggregation rules survive the phone
The four formulas stay on screen at 390px, compressed
to one line each. They are the least cuttable content
in the product: an unexplained aggregate number is
worse than no aggregate number, and a phone user is
no less entitled to the model.
HOV
CMT
L/G
Structure phase, grayscale by discipline. Colour, type
scale, glyph artwork and motion curves are deferred to the
visual-design phase; tick tuning, persistence and the text
corpus are deferred to implementation. Both deferral lists
are enumerated in 00-BRIEF.md section 5 and BUILD-SPEC.md
section 9. Worked type: ISTP (Ti / Se / Ni / Fe). Worked
scenario: The Credit Thief.
